people.imagined: The painting table in the small hours, a single tall silver candle burning beside her. She has sat so still over the page that three moths have settled on her sleeve, and she does not move them. A brush is poised a hair above the paper.
people.subject: The moment: in the small hours she sits motionless at a low painting table, a single tall silver candle burning beside her, a brush held a hair above the paper; she has sat so still that three pale moths have settled on her sleeve and she does not move them. Face: a slight, fine-boned, serene face of about fifty-five with high small cheekbones, calm pale-grey eyes lowered to the page, thin straight grey brows, a small straight nose, a gentle closed mouth, very fine lightly lined skin and a faint smudge of soot on one temple. Hair: pure grey, fine and straight, drawn back into a low knot at the nape and crowned with a small jet crown-clasp and a long jet hairpin, a slim bamboo brush thrust through the knot. Body: slight, small-shouldered, utterly upright and still, the stillness of long practice. Clothing: the richest dress of the Hall for its mistress, three layers of matte black silk with crossed collars edged in a faint violet sheen, over them a wide-sleeved over-robe of black gauze painted with faint silver talisman lines that hold no writing, narrow cuffs embroidered with silver Dipper-dots, a black silk cord at the left wrist and a sash hung with a black jade disc; the whole falls in long still folds. Hands and objects: the right hand holds a slender brush of dark wood poised over a long strip of pale paper bearing seven small black dots in the shape of a ladle; the left rests flat beside a small black gourd of ink; a tall silver candlestick with a white wax candle at the table's edge; three pale moths on the black sleeve. Background: a bare dark room with a single high window and shelves of rolled paper, blurred in drifting incense mist. Light: the candle from the upper right, a soft warm circle on her face and the paper, with a cold silver moon-rim on her hair. Power: a Kết Đan mistress, so a soft green Wood glow gathers at the brush tip and silver-green motes drift upward from the paper like fireflies. Expression: still, devoted, eyes lowered to the paper. Palette: black, candle gold, soft grey, pale green.

people.imagined: The Hall's great painting room at midday. She is talking while she paints, which no one else dares, a boxwood seal swinging on its cord, ink to the elbow, mid-sentence about a price.
people.subject: The moment: at midday in the Hall's great painting room she paints rapidly at a long table while talking over her shoulder to someone out of frame, brush flying, mid-sentence about a price, a boxwood seal swinging on its cord. Face: a long, lively, handsome face of about forty with a strong jaw, quick dark eyes under thick arched brows, a long nose, a wide mobile mouth caught mid-word and a black ink streak across the cheek. Hair: black, in a high knot pierced by two slim brushes and a jet hairpin, a loose strand at the temple. Body: tall, long-limbed, leaning over the table with one hip against its edge, restless energy in every angle. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk in two layers with crossed collars and a narrow violet band at the cuff, the wide sleeves pushed up to the elbow and the forearms ink-black from wrist to elbow, an over-sash of black gauze painted with a few silver talisman lines, a black cord at the left wrist; the rich dress of the chief painter. Hands and objects: a brush in the right hand mid-stroke over a strip of yellow paper marked with seven dots; on a cord at her chest a small boxwood seal carved with seven dots, swinging; a row of seven brushes in a stand. Background: a long bright painting room with rows of tables and dozens of bowed painters, rolled papers hung on a line to dry, blurred in soft mist. Light: bright pale daylight from tall windows on the upper left, with a silver-white rim on her hair. Power: a faint pale green Wood glow gathers at the brush tip and a few green motes spark off the wet ink. Expression: quick, bright, eager eyes and a mouth already shaping the next word. Palette: ink black, paper yellow, violet.

people.imagined: The cabinet of a thousand ink sticks in his kiln-house. He has pulled one stick out, sniffed it, and is naming its year before reading the label, with a stubborn old smile through his burnt eyebrows.
people.subject: The moment: in the cabinet room of a thousand ink sticks in his kiln-house, he holds a black ink stick to his nose in front of a huge cabinet of small drawers, eyes closed, lips moving as he names its year before reading the label, with a stubborn old smile. Face (most important: black hands and burnt eyebrows): a lined, leathery old face of about seventy with a big hooked nose, deep-set black eyes, bald spots where the eyebrows were burnt away leaving only a few singed stubs, a wide stubborn mouth, grey stubble and soot-smudged cheeks. Hair: thin grey, in a knot bound with a black silk cloth and a plain jet pin. Body: stocky, short, bent forward, broad strong shoulders, a charcoal burner's frame. Clothing: a robe of matte black silk in two layers, soot-dusted but clean, with crossed collars edged in a faint violet sheen, the wide sleeves rolled to the elbow, an over-robe of black gauze painted with faint silver talisman lines, a black cord at the left wrist, a broad black sash hung with a small jet disc. Hands and objects: both hands black to the wrist as if dipped in ink; in the right a long black ink stick with a gold mark; before him a wall cabinet of a thousand tiny drawers each with a small paper tag; a lamp on a hook. Background: the cabinet rows and a kiln-house with a glowing mouth seen through an arch, blurred, warm smoke. Light: orange kiln glow from the lower right and a warm lamp from the upper left, with a pale silver rim on his bald crown. Power: a faint dark-green Wood haze of pine smoke curls round the ink stick and a few green motes drift up. Expression: eyes shut, nose lifted, a mouth that holds a secret. Palette: black, kiln orange, grey.

people.imagined: The archive courtyard in the city, his one day a month. He stands neat and soft-spoken in Pivot grey with a black cord at his wrist, glancing back over his shoulder at the archive windows, wanting to walk home.
people.subject: The moment: in the archive courtyard in the city, on his one day a month, he stands neat and soft-spoken in Pivot grey, a small package of ink sticks under his arm, glancing back over his shoulder at the archive windows, wanting to walk home. Face: a neat, soft, pleasant face of about forty with kind brown eyes, level mild brows, a small nose, a small closed mouth, a clean-shaven chin and faint ink on the left thumb. Hair: black, combed and tied in a neat topknot under a small grey gauze cap with a jet pin. Body: slight, narrow-shouldered, upright, a clerk's careful posture. Clothing: a robe of Pivot grey silk in two layers, the crossed collar high and closed at the chin, narrow sleeves under a pale grey over-robe of fine gauze, borders embroidered in the faintest violet thread with seven small dots, a neat grey sash; at the left wrist a black silk cord tied in a flat knot, the one mark of the Hall. Hands and objects: a long flat parcel of black ink sticks wrapped in blue silk under the left arm; in the right hand a small brass key; ink on the left thumb. Background: a stone courtyard with an arched gate, rows of identical windows of a tall archive building, a few clerks in grey, drifting mist, blurred. Light: soft cool spirit-light from the upper left with a pale silver rim on his cap and shoulder. Power: a faint pale-green Wood shimmer rests on the wrapped ink sticks and a few green motes hang near his hand. Expression: a gentle backward glance, brows drawn a little, a wistful mouth. Palette: archive grey, ink black, cloth blue.

people.imagined: The dye vats of the village at dusk, steam rising violet. She stands with her arms folded and her purse inside her sash, where no one has ever seen it open, adding up the price of the violet in her head.
people.subject: The moment: at dusk before the dye vats of the village, steam rising violet, she stands with her arms folded and her purse inside her sash, where no one has ever seen it open, adding up the price of the violet in her head. Face: a broad, practical, sun-browned face of about forty-five with sharp small eyes, thick straight brows, a short nose, a thin mouth pulled tight in thought and a smear of violet on the chin. Hair: black with some grey, in a tight bun wrapped in a black silk head-cloth and held with a jet hairpin. Body: stocky, square, strong, planted wide. Clothing: a robe of matte black silk with two crossed collars edged in violet, the wide sleeves rolled and tied back, a black cord at the left wrist, a broad belt-like sash of black brocade wound tight round the waist hiding a flat purse, a violet-stained silk over-skirt; the steady dress of a keeper of the Hall's village. Hands and objects: both hands violet to the second knuckle, folded at the elbow; behind her a vat of deep violet liquid with a wooden paddle and steam; a stack of dyed grey paper drying on a rack; a dark fungus the size of a plate on a board. Background: a village of low sooty houses at the foot of pines, smoke from several vats and a long line of dyed cloth, blurred. Light: low violet-pink dusk light from the left, the steam glowing, a faint silver rim on her bun. Power: a faint pale-violet Wood haze drifts in the steam and a few green-violet motes rise with it. Expression: shrewd narrowed eyes, mouth shut tight over the figures. Palette: violet, black, dusk pink.

people.imagined: The head's room in the early morning. She sweeps the floor with a stoop, and when the head turns away she smiles a beat after everyone else has stopped, calculating what she may take from the Silver Candle's teaching.
people.subject: The moment: in the head's room in the early morning she sweeps the floor with a stoop, and as the head turns away she looks up and smiles a beat after everyone else has stopped, weighing what she may take from the Silver Candle's teaching. Face: a young, round, pleasant face of about twenty-four with soft brown eyes, short straight brows, a small nose, a small pink mouth whose smile arrives late and stays too long, and a smudge of dust on the forehead. Hair: black, in a plain bun tied with a black silk cord and a slim bamboo brush thrust through it. Body: sturdy and small, stooping as she sweeps, shoulders rounded. Clothing: the Hall's simple matte black silk, two crossed collars edged in the faintest violet, sleeves tied back by a black silk cord at the wrist, a short black over-skirt and plain black silk shoes with a dusty hem; graceful and unadorned, the dress of an inner disciple. Hands and objects: both hands on a long-handled broom of twigs; beside her on the floor a small black ink stone and a bundle of brushes; in the corner a tall silver candlestick with a white candle, glowing. Background: a bare dark room with a low painting table, a high window, rolled papers on a shelf, drifting dust motes in the light, blurred. Light: pale early light from the window at the upper left and a thin gold line from the candle, a soft silver rim on her cheek. Power: a faint pale-green Wood glimmer follows the broom and a few green motes lift from the dust. Expression: a bright, deferential smile that comes a beat late, eyes already looking elsewhere. Palette: black, candle gold, dust grey.

people.imagined: The Hall's painting room, midday. In a place where everyone else's cuffs are black with ink his are perfectly clean, and he is painting the seventh star with a calm, almost lazy steadiness.
people.subject: The moment: in the Hall's painting room at midday, in a place where everyone else's cuffs are black with ink his are perfectly clean, he sits at a table painting the seventh star with a calm, almost lazy steadiness. Face: a smooth, mild, handsome young face of about twenty with large calm dark eyes, soft level brows, a straight nose, a faint idle smile and no smudge anywhere. Hair: black, in a neat knot with a slim brush through it. Body: lean and relaxed, leaning back a little with one elbow on the table. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk in two layers with crossed collars edged in violet, spotless cuffs and sleeves rolled up neatly twice, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a plain black sash with a small jet bead; the cleanest garment in the room, the graceful dress of an inner disciple. Hands and objects: a thin brush held in the right hand over a strip of paper that has six dots already and a space for the seventh; the hands themselves clean; a small cake of pine nuts wrapped in a leaf on the table, a stack of finished strips beside. Background: the long painting room with rows of painters bent over tables, all with black cuffs, drifting mist, blurred. Light: bright pale window light from the upper left, a silver-white rim along his jaw. Power: a faint pale-green Wood glow gathers at the brush tip and one bright green mote hangs where the seventh dot will go. Expression: a lazy half-smile and easy half-lidded eyes. Palette: black, paper yellow, soft green.

people.imagined: On the sloping roof of a soot kiln at noon, black from hair to heel, singing off-key as she scrapes soot into a basket. Her teeth are the only white thing about her.
people.subject: The moment: on the sloping roof of a soot kiln at noon, black from hair to heel, she sings off-key as she scrapes soot into a basket. Face (most important: black with soot, her teeth the only white thing): a round, cheerful face entirely blackened with soot, white teeth in a huge grin, bright black eyes with white corners and round cheeks; about seventeen. Hair: black, in two rough braids coated in soot and tied with black silk cord. Body: sturdy and strong-armed, standing wide and easy on the sloping roof. Clothing: the Hall's black silk, a robe with crossed collars whose sleeves and hem are caked with soot, a black cord at the left wrist, a short black work-skirt over wide trousers, bare feet blackened; the soot is the story here, the cut remains graceful and the violet edge at the collar still shows through. Hands and objects: a flat iron scraper in the right hand; a wide basket of fine black soot on her hip; a cloth tied over the nose pushed down to her chin; a small oil lamp on a hook. Background: the kiln mouths glowing red, a slope of tall vermilion-trunked pines, thick dark smoke rising, blurred. Light: bright pale spirit-light from the upper left with a silver rim on her braids, and an orange kiln glow from below. Power: a faint soft green Wood glimmer drifts in the smoke around her and a few green motes flicker in the soot. Expression: a wide singing mouth and shining eyes. Palette: soot black, pine red, white teeth.

people.imagined: The archive courtyard, a copyists' stall. He laughs so loudly that heads turn across the courtyard, one ear always inked, handing a cup of wine to a copyist and trading a little too much gossip for it.
people.subject: The moment: at a copyists' stall in the archive courtyard he laughs so loudly, head thrown back, that heads turn across the courtyard, a cup of wine in his hand, trading a little too much gossip for it. Face (most important: one inked ear): a round, merry, red-cheeked face of about nineteen with crinkled bright eyes, a wide laughing mouth, a snub nose and a right ear stained black with ink as if dipped; the laughing mouth shows a gap in the lower teeth. Hair: black, tousled, tied in a knot with a grey silk cloth. Body: stocky and lively, one foot up on the stall rail, a swagger in the shoulders. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk robe with crossed collars edged in violet, the sleeves tied back, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a Pivot-grey over-sash, ink at the cuffs; graceful, with a jade bead on the sash. Hands and objects: a small clay wine cup raised in the right hand; a long ink stick with a gold stripe in the left; a pouch of ink sticks hanging at his belt. Background: a courtyard of stalls with copyists at low desks and a tall grey archive wall, drifting mist, blurred. Light: bright pale daylight from the upper left, the black ear standing out sharp against the pale wall, a silver rim on his hair. Power: a faint pale-green Wood shimmer rides the gold-striped ink stick and one or two green motes jump from the wine. Expression: a loud open laugh and eyes squeezed shut with glee. Palette: black, archive grey, wine red.

people.imagined: On the fungus slope, a small dark-eyed girl re-pinning a twig of deer-grass in her hair for the hundredth time, nose wrinkled at a smell that tells her a glue yard is boiling somewhere nearby.
people.subject: The moment: on the fungus slope a small dark-eyed girl is re-pinning a twig of deer-grass in her hair for the hundredth time, her nose wrinkled at a smell on the wind that tells her a glue yard is boiling somewhere nearby. Face: a small, dark-eyed, serious face of about sixteen with large dark eyes, fine straight brows, a small nose wrinkled up and a small anxious mouth. Hair: black, long, in a loose braid with a twig of pale deer-grass pinned at the side of the head. Body: small, slight and light-footed, shoulders narrow. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk robe with crossed collars edged in violet, shortened at the hem for walking, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a small satchel for fungus, soft cloth shoes; the sleeve is dusted with spore powder; the simple graceful dress of an outer disciple. Hands and objects: the left hand reaching up to the twig in her hair; the right holding a flat basket of dark grey fungus the size of saucers, a few caps lying with their gills showing pale; a small knife at her belt. Background: a damp slope of dark pines with pale fungus on logs, a little meadow below with a single deer lifting its head, a faint column of smoke from a yard, blurred in mist. Light: soft green-grey spirit-light from the upper left, a faint silver rim on her braid. Power: a faint pale-green Wood shimmer gathers over the basket and a few spore motes drift in the light. Expression: a wrinkled nose and worried, sincere eyes. Palette: grey fungus, black, meadow green.

people.imagined: The year she founded the Hall in 910: a short fungus-dyer's daughter with violet nails, a brush in each hand, painting the seven stars of the Dipper on a long scroll with both hands at once.
people.subject: The moment: memorial portrait, faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened; the year she founded the Hall in 910, a short fungus-dyer's daughter with violet nails holds a brush in each hand, painting the seven stars of the Dipper on a long scroll with both hands at once, looking up with fierce calm. Face: a broad, short-jawed, firm face of about forty-five with sharp black eyes, thick straight brows, a short nose, a closed wide mouth and deep lines at the eyes. Hair: black, in a tight topknot with two brushes thrust through it and a plain jet hairpin. Body: short, stocky, strong-shouldered, planted wide. Clothing: the earliest form of the Hall's black, a robe of plain dark-grey silk in two layers with crossed collars, a black silk sash, sleeves rolled and tied, a long over-skirt stained with ink and violet dye; strong and dignified rather than rich, the founder's first design, with a faint violet sheen at the collar. Hands and objects: a brush in each hand, one dipped in black and the other in red; every fingernail stained a deep violet, clearly visible; a long scroll of pale paper before her with seven dots in the shape of a ladle; a small black pot of ink and a lump of ink stick. Background: a dim room with a tall window onto pines and a cabinet of small tools, blurred in mist. Light: soft pale spirit-light from the upper left, the whole picture aged and softened, a faint silver rim on her hair. Power: a faint violet shimmer gathers at her fingers and a few violet motes rise from the wet strokes. Expression: fierce, steady eyes raised from the scroll, a closed firm mouth. Palette: faded black, violet, old paper.

people.imagined: Among the vermilion pines at the kilns, she raps her tapping-rod on the ground before she speaks, counting the trees the kilns have burned, her thumb yellow with pitch.
people.subject: The moment: among the vermilion pines at the kilns she raps her tapping-rod on the ground and looks hard at someone before she speaks, counting the trees the kilns have burned. Face (most important: the pitch-yellow thumb): a lean, tough, sun-browned face of about forty-five with a long straight nose, narrow grey eyes, firm straight brows and a thin mouth set honestly; the right thumb stained deep yellow-brown with pitch, held up against the rod. Hair: black with grey streaks, in a tight bun under a straw hat tied with a black silk cord and a jet pin. Body: lean, straight, a long stride, shoulders squared. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk, a robe with two crossed collars edged in violet, kilted at the knee for the woods over trousers, a black cord at the left wrist, a gauze over-robe painted with a few faint silver talisman lines, resin-spotted at the hem, strong cloth boots; the dress of a steward of Trúc Cơ standing. Hands and objects: a long tapping-rod of dark wood with an iron tip in the right hand; a small gourd of resin at the belt; a tally of notched sticks in a pouch. Background: tall vermilion-trunked pines in rows, each with a scarred tapping-cut, a thin trail of smoke from a kiln, drifting mist, blurred. Light: shafts of low gold spirit-light through the trunks from the upper left, a silver rim on her hat brim. Power: a faint soft green Wood glow lingers in the pine bark and a few resin-gold motes drift in the shafts of light. Expression: a level, hard stare, mouth set honestly. Palette: pine red, black, resin amber.

people.imagined: The painting table, the smell of the kilns heavy in the air, a dried persimmon in his sleeve against it. He paints with his left hand, calm and stubborn, a letter from his friend's mother waiting in his sash.
people.subject: The moment: at the painting table with the smell of the kilns heavy in the air, a dried persimmon peeking from his right sleeve against it, he paints with his left hand, absorbed, a letter from his friend's mother waiting in his sash. Face: a steady, square face of about forty with level brown eyes, strong straight brows, a straight nose, a closed firm mouth and a clean-shaven chin. Hair: black, in a tidy knot slightly off-centre with a slim brush through it, a grey hair or two at the temple. Body: broad and steady, sitting upright with a lean toward the left hand. Clothing: a robe of matte black silk in two layers with crossed collars edged in violet, the cuffs inked to the wrist, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a black over-sash of gauze with a few faint silver lines, a plain jet bead; from the right sleeve peeks a round orange dried persimmon; rich enough for a master painter of the middle stars. Hands and objects: a thin brush in the left hand over a strip of paper with dots in the shape of the Dipper's middle stars; the right hand flat on the table; a folded letter tied with red thread in the sash. Background: the painting room with tables and painters bent over, a high window, drifting mist, blurred. Light: pale window light from the upper left, the orange of the persimmon the only warm colour in the black room, a faint silver rim on his knot. Power: a faint pale-green Wood glow gathers at the brush tip and one green mote rests on the paper. Expression: eyes on the brush, a closed, stubborn mouth. Palette: black, persimmon orange, paper yellow.

people.imagined: The kiln mouths at night, counting them twice with his lips moving, a cracked front tooth showing, half sure the fault is in the soot and not his hand, watching the boys' hands.
people.subject: The moment: at night before a row of glowing kiln mouths, he counts them twice with his lips moving, half sure the fault is in the soot and not his hand, watching the boys' hands. Face (most important: the cracked front tooth): a sharp, thin, tense face of about nineteen with narrow suspicious dark eyes, thick straight brows, a long nose and a mouth parted in the count to show a front tooth with a visible crack through it; soot streaks his cheeks and a thread of sweat cuts through it at the temple. Hair: black, short and bristling, soot on the forehead. Body: wiry, tight-shouldered, stiff and watchful. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk robe with crossed collars edged in violet, sleeves rolled, a black cord at the left wrist, a scorched black work-skirt over wide trousers, boots; the cut is graceful beneath the scorching. Hands and objects: a long iron poker in the right hand; the left held up with the fingers counting; a lantern hanging from a hook at his side; a strip of yellow talisman paper smeared with a run of ink tucked in his belt. Background: four kiln mouths glowing orange in a row, smoke, dark pines beyond, blurred. Light: orange kiln light from the lower left on the face, the glow reflected in each of his narrowed eyes, a faint silver rim on his hair. Power: a faint dark-green Wood haze rolls through the kiln smoke and a few green motes ride it up. Expression: a tight, suspicious stare, lips moving over the count. Palette: kiln orange, black, ash grey.

people.imagined: At the dye vats in the steam, coughing as the vapour turns. Dyed blue-black to the wrist, she has asked only to be left here and never taught to paint, and she hums, content.
people.subject: The moment: at the dye vats in the steam, coughing as the vapour turns, one hand pressed to her mouth and the other stirring a black cord in the dye; dyed blue-black to the wrist, she has asked only to be left here and never taught to paint, and hums, content. Face: a soft, pale, round face of about seventeen with small close-set kind eyes, soft brows, a button nose, a small mouth and cheeks flushed by steam. Hair: black, in a loose bun under a silk cloth wrapped round the head, damp wisps sticking to her cheeks. Body: small, round-shouldered, patient, a slight stoop, narrow shoulders and thin wrists with a fine tremor of cough through the ribs. Clothing: the Hall's black silk, a short-sleeved robe with crossed collars edged in violet, let down at the hem and edged with a lighter black band, a black cord at the left wrist, a damp black over-skirt splashed with fungus-grey and violet; graceful, a little too big. Hands and objects: both hands dyed blue-black to the wrist, plainly visible; the right holding a long wooden paddle lifting a dripping black cord from the vat; a rack of cords drying behind. Background: several racks of black cord and cloth hanging in dripping rows, a stack of grey logs with fungus beside a stone trough, blurred in steam. Light: soft damp spirit-light from the upper left, steam glowing faintly violet, a pale shaft giving the vat's surface a violet sheen. Power: a faint pale violet-green Wood hint drifts in the steam and a few pale motes turn with it. Expression: a content hum on her lips and half-closed eyes, a little ill. Palette: blue-black, steam grey, violet.

people.imagined: A painter's corridor, a kiln boy paying her a copper to be let off carrying her brushes, the two brass hairpins in her hair not Hall issue. She holds out a hand, her chin high.
people.subject: The moment: in a painter's corridor a kiln boy out of frame pays her a copper to be let off carrying her brushes, and she holds out a hand, her chin high, looking down her nose at him. Face: a pretty, sharp, proud face of about twenty-two with narrow dark heavy-lidded eyes, thin arched brows, a straight nose and a thin mouth turned in disdain. Hair: black, in a high knot with two shiny brass hairpins in the shape of small leaves, clearly not the Hall's plain bamboo brushes. Body: slender, tall for her age, upright, hips tilted in a swagger. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk, neat and well cut, two crossed collars with a violet edge, slim sleeves with a violet band at the cuff, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a thin chain of brass at the neck, a smudge of green pigment on the left sleeve; the most fashionable cut an inner disciple can manage. Hands and objects: the right palm open, held out for the copper; the left holds a bundle of seven brushes wrapped in a black silk cloth; a small bag at the belt. Background: a dim corridor with paper lanterns and a row of closed doors, a small kiln boy half in frame, blurred. Light: lantern light from the upper left, brass glints in her hair and a faint silver rim on her cheek. Power: a faint pale-green Wood glimmer follows the wrapped brushes and a bright mote winks in the brass. Expression: chin high, eyes sweeping the boy from boots to collar with a hard proud gleam, a grasping set to the mouth. Palette: ink-black, bronze, amethyst.

people.imagined: The archive courtyard, sitting on a step with the Hall's book on his knee, copying ink orders. His left sleeve is inked to the elbow, and he looks up earnestly when his master asks for a page of 1195.
people.subject: The moment: in the archive courtyard he sits on a stone step with the Hall's book on his knee, copying ink orders with a brush, and looks up earnestly at his master out of frame, who has asked for a page of 1195. Face: a young, round, honest face of about eighteen with large trusting brown eyes, soft brows, a short nose, an open mouth and ink on one cheek. Hair: black, in a short topknot tied with a grey silk cloth, a cowlick standing up at the back of the head. Body: slight and earnest, hunched over the book like a heron's neck, knees apart, shoulders pitched forward, the book propped on his thigh. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk robe with crossed collars edged in violet, the right sleeve clean and the left blotched with ink black to the elbow, both cuffs tied with black cord, a black silk cord at the left wrist, a small satchel at the belt with a ruler and an ink stick; the plain graceful dress of an outer disciple. Hands and objects: a thin brush in the right hand; the book open on his knee with ruled columns of small plain strokes; a small ink stone at his side; the left forearm black to the elbow. Background: a stone archive courtyard with a tall grey wall and tall windows in a regular grid, a wooden bench with other boys, a clay water jar by the step, copyists in the distance, blurred in mist. Light: bright pale spirit-light from above and the upper left, a small sharp shadow under the book, a silver rim on his hair. Power: a faint pale-green Wood shimmer follows the brush strokes and one green mote rests on the page. Expression: wide trusting eyes lifted to his master, mouth a little open. Palette: black, archive grey, paper cream.

people.imagined: The deer meadow of Lộc Uyển, with his white forelock he blames on a stag. He stands among grazing deer, smelling faintly of them, refusing in his heart to paint with deer glue.
people.subject: The moment: in the deer meadow of Lộc Uyển he stands among grazing deer, his hand resting on a hind's neck, looking steadily at the viewer, with the white forelock he blames on a stag, smelling faintly of them and refusing in his heart to paint with deer glue. Face (most important: a white forelock): an honest, quiet, lean face of about twenty-one with steady brown eyes, level brows, a straight nose, a closed mouth and a streak of pure white hair at the front of the black hair like a stag's blaze. Hair: black with a prominent white forelock, tied back in a short tail with a black silk cord and a plain jet pin. Body: lean, easy and still, with the soft movements of someone used to animals. Clothing: the Hall's matte black silk robe with crossed collars edged in violet, shortened at the hem, a black cord at the left wrist, a small satchel, boots with meadow mud; a few pale deer hairs cling to the sleeve; the graceful dress of an outer disciple. Hands and objects: the left hand resting flat on a deer's neck; the right holding a small fungus basket; a gourd at the belt.
